sub_agendas_items.title: Chair of the Board of Health Verbal Report
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
In her verbal report, the Chair thanked Métis Elder Senator Parm Burgie for opening the meeting in a special way. The Chair then provided recap of the  Association of Local Public Health Agencies’ (alPHa) Fall Symposiu, which she and Vice Chair DeGiovanni recently attended as well as a recap of the Health and Housing Forum that occurred earlier in the day. The Chair informed the Board of events that took place in the City in recognition of World 
The Chair then highlighted AIDS Awareness Day and some holiday messaging, including tips for protecting ourselves against the respiratory illnesses circulating in our community. 
Discussions on this item lasted approximately 5 minutes. The Board then voted to RECEIVE the Chair's Verbal Report.

motions.motion_text: That the Board of Health for the City of Ottawa Health Unit receive this verbal report for information.

sub_agendas_items.title: Medical Officer of Health Verbal Report
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Dr. Etches began her verbal report by recognizing Senator Parm Burgie and thanked her for her opening the last meeting of the 2024 Board of Health in such a special way.
Next Dr. Etches provided a staffing update, and welcomed Hindia Mohamoud, the new permanent Program Manager for the Health Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (HEDI) service area at Ottawa Public Health (OPH).
Dr. Etches provided a heartfelt thank you and expressed gratitude to every Ottawa Public Health team member for their care, dedication, and hard work throughout 2024 and provided a look ahead to 2025 and the ways in which OPH’s work will be guided by its multi-year strategic objectives. 
Dr. Etches provided an update on the drug toxicity crisis and advised that since the provincial announcement of the consumption and treatment service closures, OPH will continue to collaborate closely with partners under Ottawa’s Overdose Prevention and Response Strategy, and with residents and businesses in communities most affected.
In closing Dr. Etches shared holiday messaging and encouraged residents to look after their health and well-being by staying up to date on vaccinations, practice good hygiene, stay active and eat well, and to be mindful of mental health. 
Following her verbal report, Dr. Etches responded to questions from Board Members. 
Discussions on this item lasted approximately 16 minutes. The Board then voted to RECEIVE the Medical Officer of Health's Verbal Report.

motions.motion_text: That the Board of Health for the City of Ottawa Health Unit receive this verbal report for information.
